tool.name: Manipulation
tool.description: utility that parses and transforms text using regular expressions (sed)

param.name: pattern
param.label: the pattern
param.help: here you can enter your sed expression (No syntax check or sanitising!)

tool.help:
**Warning: use with caution!** This is a plain wrapper around **sed** and the pattern you enter is not sanitized, so it is passed to the shell as-is. A malformed or malicious pattern can break the tool run.
-----
**What it does**
Changes every line of a text file according to a given regular expression.
-----
**Syntax**
Use the **sed** syntax -> `s/find-pattern/replace-pattern/`
The wrapper always passes `-r`, so you can use extended regular expressions (`(`, `)`, `+`, `?`, `|`, `{...}`) without escaping them.
**Examples**
- `s/x/-/` Replace all `x` with `-`. - `s/_.*//` Splits a string after `_` and replaces the rest with nothing. - `s/[^_]*_*//` Splits a string after `_` and replaces the first part with nothing. - `s/\s.*//` Splits a string after whitespaces and replaces the rest with nothing. - `s/\S*\s*//` Splits a string after whitespaces and replaces the first part with nothing.
Several commands can be chained with `;`, for example `s/sample/SMP/; s/_01//`.
-----
**Sandbox mode**
This wrapper always runs **sed** in sandbox mode (`--sandbox`, available since GNU sed 4.3). In sandbox mode the `r` (read from file), `w` (write to file) and `e` (execute shell command) sed commands are rejected, which stops an expression from reading or writing arbitrary files on the Galaxy worker. If your expression needs those commands, this tool cannot be used for it.
A malformed expression makes **sed** exit with an error, which fails the Galaxy job rather than producing truncated output.
